unit: one semantic event; one previous relevant event is allowed only to resolve a reference or prior commitment; no full deal history and no later event
general_rules: Classify only what the current event explicitly establishes, using the supplied previous related event only as local context.
If the supplied event and local context do not establish the YES criterion, answer NO; do not guess from silence, elapsed time or deal state.
Do not infer customer speech from a seller proposal, CRM task title, or unsupported manager speculation.
Extracted fields must be short normalized source-grounded phrases; use null when a field is not stated.
Never infer deal result, a whole-deal current state, the latest gate, or counts of missed commitments.

classifiers.name: CUSTOMER_COMMITMENT
classifiers.question: Does the customer explicitly commit themselves or a customer-side person/team to a concrete future action?
classifiers.yes_rule: An explicit customer-side owner undertakes a concrete future action. A date is useful but not required if the action is concrete.
classifiers.no_rule: Seller plans or offers an action, or customer uses only vague possibility such as look, think, maybe or try without a concrete customer-owned action.

field_rules.owner: customer person or role explicitly stated; null if first-person owner is clear but unnamed
field_rules.due_at_or_expected_result: normalized explicit date, event or expected result; null if absent

classifiers.name: COMMITMENT_COMPLETION
classifiers.question: Does the customer explicitly report that a previously agreed customer-side action has been completed?
classifiers.yes_rule: The customer explicitly reports completion of the action established in the previous related event, or explicitly identifies it as a previously agreed action in the current event.
classifiers.no_rule: No explicit completion report; seller says they completed their own task; action merely planned; a file exists without an attributable customer completion statement.

field_rules.completed_action: short description of the completed customer-side action

classifiers.name: COMMITMENT_RESCHEDULE
classifiers.question: Does the customer explicitly move a previously agreed customer-side action to a new time, event, or expected checkpoint?
classifiers.yes_rule: The customer explicitly changes the checkpoint of an already agreed customer-side action; the new checkpoint is stated.
classifiers.no_rule: A new unrelated plan, seller rescheduling their own call, vague postponement without a new checkpoint, or no prior agreed action.

field_rules.new_due_at_or_expected_result: short normalized new date, event or expected result

classifiers.name: EXPLICIT_MISS
classifiers.question: Does the event explicitly establish that a previously agreed customer-side action was not completed as promised?
classifiers.yes_rule: Customer or a clearly sourced report explicitly says the agreed customer-side action was not completed by the promise, with the previous agreement identifiable.
classifiers.no_rule: Only silence, a passed deadline, missing documentation, an unanswered call, a seller guess or an unrelated delay.

classifiers.name: DECISION_GATE_FACT
classifiers.question: Does this event state a concrete fact about an internal customer decision gate?
classifiers.yes_rule: The event explicitly ties at least one fact to a particular internal customer review, approval, financing or procurement decision gate.
classifiers.no_rule: Generic interest or decision language without a particular internal gate; seller's next step; a role mentioned without an internal decision context.

field_rules.customer_role: explicit customer-side decision role, otherwise null
field_rules.decision_action: specific action for this gate, otherwise null; generic think/look/decide is null
field_rules.checkpoint: bounded date, event or expected result for this same gate, otherwise null

classifiers.name: CHECKABLE_TECHNICAL_REQUIREMENT
classifiers.question: Does the customer state an application-specific technical requirement, constraint, or question that can be evaluated, tested, calculated, or answered against the proposed solution?
classifiers.yes_rule: Customer-stated, application-specific and checkable technical content is present in the current event.
classifiers.no_rule: General interest, seller's suggestion, generic equipment category, or a technical fact with no customer-stated requirement, constraint or answerable question.

label_record.fields: all fields_if_yes keys for this classifier, each string or null; empty object if no fields; for NO use nulls
